tool_args.rationale: All five observations are positive and lie at H = 0.16–0.48. Over that window, a slow exponential is approximately linear in H, so its amplitude and timescale can trade off while implying very different long-horizon responses. A long-horizon probe directly tests whether the sink-inhibited response persists or is overtaken by slow adaptation.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Finer short-window sampling could resolve fast transients but would not directly constrain the slow response at the forecast horizon.
The pilot supports sink inhibition but cannot establish that the response is independent of horizon.
The five short-window observations do not separately constrain the slow amplitude and timescale well enough to forecast at H = 22.2.
